'''Yasuo Akizuki''' (23 August 1902 – 11 July 1984) was a Japanese [[mathematician]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=e6jrCAAAQBAJ|title=Miscellanea Mathematica|first1=M.|last1=Atiyah|author-link=Michael Atiyah|first2=F.L.|last2=Bauer|first3=H.|last3=Cartan|author-link3=Henri Cartan|first4=S.-S.|last4=Chern|author-link4=Chern|first5=F.|last5=Hirzebruch|author-link5=Friedrich Hirzebruch|first6=J.H.|last6=Conway|author-link6=J. H. Conway|first7=B.|last7=Eckmann|first8=L.D.|last8=Faddeev|first9=Reinhold|last9=Remmert|author-link9=Reinhold Remmert|first10=H.|last10=Grauert|author-link10=Hans Grauert|first11=H.|last11=Hironaka|author-link11=Heisuke Hironaka|first12=L.|last12=Hörmander|author-link12=Lars Hörmander|first13=F.|last13=John|first14=M.|last14=Koecher|first15=R.|last15=Narasimhan|first16=C.|last16=Reid|first17=J-P.|last17=Serre|author-link17=Jean-Pierre Serre|first18=N.J.A.|last18=Sloane|author-link18=Neil Sloane|first19=J.|last19=Tits|author-link19=Jacques Tits|first20=A.|last20=Weil|author-link20=André Weil|first21=D.|last21=Zagier|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|page=164|date=December 6, 2012|isbn=9783642767098|via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> He was a professor at [[Kyoto University]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bkBPDwAAQBAJ|title=New Trends In Stochastic Analysis: Proceedings Of The Tanaguchi International Symposium|page=7|first1=Ichiro|last1=Shigekawa|first2=K David|last2=Elworthy|first3=S|last3=Kusuoka|publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company|date=May 5, 1997|isbn=9789814547123|via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> Alongside [[Wolfgang Krull]], [[Oscar Zariski]], and [[Masayoshi Nagata]], he is famous for his early work in [[commutative algebra]]. In particular, he is most well known in helping to demonstrate [[Akizuki–Hopkins–Levitzki theorem]].

== Life ==
Yasuo Akizuki was born on 23 August 1902 in [[Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama]].
In 1926, Akizuki graduated Faculty of Mathematics, Department of Science, [[Kyoto Imperial University]].

He was inaugurated as a professor of [[Kyoto University]] in 1948.
